Definition: of Hebrew origin (H543); properly, firm, i.e. (figuratively) trustworthy; adverbially, surely (often as interjection, so be it):--amen, verily.
BiblicalUsage: Amen, firm, trustworthy, surely — and the word is the seal on everything God has said. All the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us. The whole congregation says Amen at the giving of thanks, and the unlearned man can only say it if he understands what is said. And the Bible ends with it: He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly; Amen; even so, come, Lord Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Amen is the shortest creed in the Bible, and the whole faith fits in it: God has spoken, His promises are yes in Christ, and my answer is Amen. The congregation says it together because the promises belong to all of us, and the last Amen of the Bible is a prayer, that He would come quickly. I hold that every Amen I say is a small act of trust, that what God promised He will do, and that the end of the story is not a question but an agreement.
